behavior: Chiefly nocturnal and nonmigratory. Hunts from low perches by watching or listening for prey, then pouncing or making short flights; also takes insects and bats in flight. Roosts and nests in tree cavities or nest boxes and gives whinnying calls and soft trills.
field_marks: Short, stocky body with a large head and almost no visible neck
Pointed ear tufts that can be raised or flattened
Gray, brown, or rufous plumage with dark streaks, fine barring, and pale mottling
Small hooked bill; feathered legs and strong talons
Broad, rounded wings and a short, square-tipped tail
habitat: Deciduous, mixed, or evergreen woodland with large cavity-bearing trees and some open understory; also wooded farmland, parks, and suburban landscapes, particularly near water. Avoids extensive treeless habitats.
